items.title: ERPNext Payment Entry posting failure rolls back settled square_payment_id and strands transaction in Initiated
items.evidence: execute_tokenized_payment() commits ISM Payment Transaction in status='Initiated' at L712 before charging the card via client.create_payment() at L721. In reconcile_and_post_square_payment(), Square metadata (square_payment_id, square_status, receipt_url, card_last4) is assigned in memory at L840-855, then resolve_square_accounting_config(company) (L917) and pe.insert(ignore_permissions=True); pe.submit() (L1035-1037) run with zero try/except before tx.save() (L1058) and frappe.db.commit() (L1108). Any ERPNext posting exception (closed accounting period, missing fiscal year, frozen customer, account mismatch) rolls back the entire transaction: square_payment_id is lost, tx remains permanently stuck in Initiated (blocking future RO payments via IN_FLIGHT_TX_STATUSES at L649-665), no Critical Shop Action Item is emitted, and Square webhook retries repeatedly fail with HTTP 500.
items.proposed_fix: Wrap resolve_square_accounting_config() and pe.insert()/pe.submit() (L916-1038) in a DB savepoint (frappe.db.savepoint) and try/except Exception. On error, roll back to the savepoint so the row lock and Square metadata survive, persist square_payment_id/receipt fields, set tx.status=TX_STATUS_RECONCILIATION_ERROR and tx.erpnext_sync_status='Manual Review Required', append a sanitized audit entry, emit a Critical Shop Action Item via _emit_payment_alert(), commit, and return _build_charge_result(tx).

items.title: Retryable SquareApiError (408/5xx) marks transaction Failed instead of Pending, enabling double charges
items.evidence: SquareClient._handle_response() (square_client.py:45, 254, 281) flags HTTP 408/429/500/502/503/504 (including non-JSON gateway 502/504 responses where Square may have already captured funds) as SquareApiError(..., retryable=True). Yet execute_tokenized_payment() at erpnext_bridge.py:749-767 catches every _is_square_api_error(exc) without checking exc.retryable or exc.status_code, unconditionally setting tx_doc.status=TX_STATUS_FAILED and raising ValidationError. Because Failed is not in IN_FLIGHT_TX_STATUSES, the caller can immediately retry with a new idempotency_key and double-charge the customer.
items.proposed_fix: In erpnext_bridge.py:749, check whether exc is an indeterminate gateway error (getattr(exc, 'retryable', False) and getattr(exc, 'status_code', None) in (408, 500, 502, 503, 504)). For those, transition tx_doc.status=TX_STATUS_PENDING (matching the requests.RequestException branch at L729-747) and return _build_charge_result(tx_doc) so the in-flight guard blocks duplicate charges until webhook/get_payment reconciliation. Keep definitive declines/4xx (including 429) transitioning to TX_STATUS_FAILED. [Verifier caveat: Requires human design decision before auto-fixing — returning HTTP 200 status='Pending' without a SquareClient.get_payment reconciliation/expiry job would permanently strand an RO in IN_FLIGHT_TX_STATUSES (blocking retries and cancel_deposit_request) whenever an edge 502/503 never created a Square payment.]

items.title: Out-of-order Square webhooks corrupt refund totals and resurrect Failed/Voided transactions into Pending
items.evidence: Two monotonic state-transition bugs affect out-of-order Square webhooks: (1) In _handle_refund_webhook_event() (L1228-1256), an existing refund_id entry is unconditionally overwritten at L1230-1231; if refund.created (PENDING) arrives after refund.updated (COMPLETED) with a different event_id, it overwrites status to PENDING, drops completed_refund_cents/tx.refunded_amount to 0.0 (L1244-1249), and leaves tx.status stuck at Refunded/Partially Refunded (L1252). (2) In reconcile_and_post_square_payment() (L1111-1136), the PENDING/APPROVED branch only checks 'if tx.payment_entry or tx.status == TX_STATUS_POSTED' (L1112), allowing a delayed PENDING webhook to overwrite terminal Failed/Voided/Reconciliation Error transactions back to TX_STATUS_PENDING and lock out customer retries.
items.proposed_fix: In _handle_refund_webhook_event(), enforce monotonic refund state precedence (never regress COMPLETED to PENDING/UNKNOWN) and verify currency=='CAD' before crediting refunded_amount. In reconcile_and_post_square_payment() L1112, ignore PENDING/APPROVED updates whenever tx.status is already in a terminal state (Posted, Failed, Voided, Refunded, Partially Refunded, Reconciliation Error).

notes.text: Assigned in run-002
Fixed by fixer-b (monotonic refund status precedence, CAD currency validation, and terminal tx guard on PENDING/APPROVED webhooks); verified PASS by cross-family verifier (49/49 tests on slot-3).

items.title: Race condition and full-Single ISM Settings.save() in get_portal_session_signing_secret can invalidate active OTPs and sessions
items.evidence: get_portal_session_signing_secret() (sessions.py:69-82) lazily generates portal_session_signing_secret without any DB lock and persists it via cfg.save(ignore_permissions=True) on the ISM Settings Single doc (L80-81), callable from Guest OTP (otp.py:127) and session flows (sessions.py:286). Concurrent cold-start requests both read blank, generate distinct secrets, and overwrite each other—invalidating previously issued OTP hashes/session cookies or failing with TimestampMismatchError. Additionally, full cfg.save() triggers all unrelated ISMSettings.validate() checks (ism_settings.py:34-42), so an unrelated settings validation error breaks portal auth/OTP.
items.proposed_fix: Serialize lazy secret initialization with a short MariaDB advisory lock (SELECT GET_LOCK) or row lock, re-check __Auth inside the lock, and write only portal_session_signing_secret via frappe.utils.password.set_encrypted_password() without triggering full ISMSettings.validate() under Guest context; also pre-seed the secret in ism.setup.after_install/after_migrate if blank.

items.title: TCPA compliance gap: space-separated 'OPT OUT' fails opt-out matching while conversational sentences misfire on token[0]
items.evidence: _process_inbound_message_event() (telnyx.py:617-619) only inspects the first whitespace-delimited token: first_token = raw_text.split()[0].upper(); keyword = _KEYWORD_CLEAN_RE.sub('', first_token). Although STOP_KEYWORDS (contracts.py:24-26) lists 'OPTOUT' and 'STOPALL', a customer replying with standard TCPA phrases 'OPT OUT' or 'OPT-OUT' (with space) yields keyword='OPT', which misses STOP_KEYWORDS and leaves the customer opted in. Conversely, multi-word conversational replies such as 'CANCEL my appointment' or 'YES, 3pm works' trigger unintended opt-out or opt-in transitions because only token[0] is checked. [Verifier clarification: 'STOP ALL' and hyphenated 'OPT-OUT' already match 'STOP' and 'OPTOUT' via _KEYWORD_CLEAN_RE, while space-separated 'OPT OUT' yields keyword='OPT' (missing STOP_KEYWORDS) and conversational replies like 'CANCEL my appointment' or 'YES, 3pm works' misfire on token[0].]
items.proposed_fix: Normalize the full trimmed inbound body by stripping non-alphanumeric punctuation and collapsing spaces: match exact single-word keywords (STOP_KEYWORDS / START_KEYWORDS / HELP_KEYWORDS) and canonical two-word opt-out phrases ('OPT OUT' -> 'OPTOUT', 'STOP ALL' -> 'STOPALL'), avoiding false opt-out/opt-in matches on unrelated multi-word conversational replies starting with 'CANCEL'/'END'/'YES'.

notes.text: Assigned in run-002
Fixed by fixer-b (full-body SMS normalization with canonical two-word TCPA opt-outs and conversational non-match protection); verified PASS by cross-family verifier (49/49 tests on slot-3).

items.title: is_valid_sms_webhook_url permits RFC1918 private IPs and unvalidated DNS resolution (SSRF risk)
items.evidence: is_valid_sms_webhook_url() (contracts.py:233-261) only blocks metadata.google.internal, 169.254.169.254, and literal IP addresses matching is_link_local/is_unspecified/is_multicast. It allows RFC1918 private IPs (https://10.0.0.1, https://172.16.0.1, https://192.168.1.1), IPv6 ULA, loopback HTTP even in production, and any public hostname whose DNS resolves to 169.254.169.254 or internal cluster services. CustomWebhookSMSProvider.send() (providers.py:213-219) then POSTs SMS payloads and Bearer tokens directly to that URL.
items.proposed_fix: Reject ip.is_private and ip.is_reserved in is_valid_sms_webhook_url(), restrict plain-HTTP loopback allowance to developer_mode/in_test environments, and resolve destination hostnames in CustomWebhookSMSProvider.send() via socket.getaddrinfo() to verify all resolved IPs are globally routable before sending.

items.title: upsert_sms_opt_out crashes with unhandled DuplicateEntryError on concurrent first-time STOP webhooks
items.evidence: upsert_sms_opt_out() (providers.py:411-457) locks an existing row with SELECT name FROM `tabSMS Opt Out` WHERE name = %s FOR UPDATE (L411-420), and when absent falls through to frappe.get_doc(doc_fields).insert(ignore_permissions=True) at L456. Because SMS Opt Out uses autoname='field:phone_e164' (unique=1), two concurrent STOP or carrier-error webhooks for a brand-new phone both see 0 locked rows and attempt insert(), causing the second to raise an unhandled DuplicateEntryError/UniqueValidationError and return HTTP 500 to Telnyx. [Verifier calibration (high->medium): Requires simultaneous distinct-event_id first-time webhooks for the same phone; winner commits is_opted_out=1 and Telnyx retries 5xx. Note InnoDB SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on a missing PK can also raise MariaDB deadlock (1213) alongside DuplicateEntryError.]
items.proposed_fix: Wrap the insert at providers.py:456 in a DB savepoint and catch (frappe.DuplicateEntryError, frappe.UniqueValidationError); on collision, roll back to the savepoint, re-run SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the newly inserted row, and apply the idempotent update branch. Also catch/retry MariaDB deadlock (1213) on concurrent first-insert gaps.

items.title: One-cent float tolerance allows $0.01 deposit request above remaining balance (and on $0.00 paid RO) and skips $0.01 overpayment review
items.evidence: In deposit_requests.py:165-173, 'if flt(clean_amount) > remaining + 0.01:' allows clean_amount == remaining + 0.01 because clean_amount is already quantized to exact cents. On a $100.00 RO with paid_amount=100.00 (remaining=0.0), requesting $0.01 passes '0.01 > 0.01' (False); on an unpaid $100.00 RO, $100.01 is permitted. Similarly, erpnext_bridge.py:1026 checks 'if flt(amount, 2) > si_outstanding + _AMOUNT_TOLERANCE' (_AMOUNT_TOLERANCE=0.01), silently leaving $0.01 unallocated without triggering manual_review_needed.
items.proposed_fix: Compare exact integer cents in create_deposit_request() (amount_cents > remaining_cents, rejecting any deposit when remaining_cents == 0) and in reconcile_and_post_square_payment() L1026 check 'int(tx.amount_cents) > (cad_to_cents(si_outstanding) if si_outstanding > 0 else 0)' (or 'flt(amount - si_outstanding, 2) > 0').

items.title: Guest payment rate limiter uses non-atomic Redis GET+SET and square_webhook has zero per-IP rate limiting
items.evidence: _increment_rate_limit_key() (api/payments.py:64-77) performs a non-atomic cache.get_value()+1 followed by cache.set_value(..., expires_in_sec=window_sec), allowing concurrent bursts to lose increments (bypassing per-IP/per-RO rate limits on approval_token validation and charge submission) while resetting the TTL window on every hit—unlike the atomic cache.incr()+expire pattern used in comms/otp.py:207 and api/comms_webhooks.py:26. Additionally, square_webhook() (L333-361) applies no per-IP rate limit, allowing unauthenticated floods to invoke get_single('ISM Settings') and password decryption on every request.
items.proposed_fix: Switch _increment_rate_limit_key() to atomic cache.incr(full_key) + cache.expire(full_key, window_sec) when count==1 (with safe fallback), and add a generous per-IP sanity rate limit (e.g. 300/min, returning HTTP 429) at the top of square_webhook() mirroring telnyx_webhook().

items.title: MariaDB FOR UPDATE locks held across synchronous 10s outbound SMS HTTP calls in OTP request and inbound HELP webhook
items.evidence: request_sms_otp() (comms/otp.py:464-527) acquires a FOR UPDATE lock on tabPortal OTP Challenge (L464-474), inserts the new challenge (L513), and then executes synchronous send_sms() (L516) with a 10s HTTP timeout (telnyx.py:236, providers.py:217) without releasing DB locks first. Similarly, _process_inbound_message_event() (comms/telnyx.py:580-678) holds its FOR UPDATE lock on tabSMS Audit Log across a synchronous send_sms() call for HELP keywords (L670-678). Under provider latency spikes, InnoDB row/gap locks stall concurrent auth/webhook workers.
items.proposed_fix: Commit the DB state (releasing FOR UPDATE locks) prior to external HTTP I/O in request_sms_otp() (matching erpnext_bridge.py:712), updating Delivery Failed / sms_audit_log in a follow-up short transaction, and either commit before sending or enqueue the HELP compliance reply via frappe.enqueue(..., enqueue_after_commit=True).

items.title: import_tesla_procedure allows mutating Billed/Paid, Closed/Released, and Cancelled Repair Orders
items.evidence: import_tesla_procedure() (api/tesla.py:118-236) loads the Repair Order, skips any lifecycle or invoice lock check, mutates ro.services in _apply_operations_to_ro(), and saves with ro.flags.ignore_validate_update_after_submit = True (L235-236). Neither import_tesla_procedure() nor RepairOrder.validate() blocks adding or overwriting services on a Billed / Paid, Closed / Released, Cancelled, or already-invoiced RO, allowing RO grand_total to diverge from the submitted ERPNext Sales Invoice.
items.proposed_fix: Reject import_tesla_procedure() before _upsert_service_package() with frappe.ValidationError when ro.docstatus == 2, ro.status in ('Billed / Paid', 'Closed / Released', 'Cancelled'), or a submitted Sales Invoice is linked to ro.sales_invoice.

items.title: Daily OTP and portal session cleanup jobs run unbounded SELECT ... FOR UPDATE with single-statement IN (...) clauses
items.evidence: Both cleanup_expired_otp_challenges() (comms/otp.py:887-930) and cleanup_expired_portal_sessions() (comms/sessions.py:742-785) run unbounded SELECT name ... FOR UPDATE without LIMIT and build a single UPDATE/DELETE ... WHERE name IN ({placeholders}) over every matched row. After traffic spikes or missed scheduler runs, locking and deleting thousands of rows in one statement risks MariaDB lock-wait timeouts against live auth traffic and max_allowed_packet errors.
items.proposed_fix: Batch both daily cleanup jobs in bounded chunks (e.g., LIMIT 500 per iteration, up to a sane per-run cap with per-batch commit when not in_test) so InnoDB locks stay short and IN (...) placeholder lists remain small.

items.title: State-mutating whitelisted payment and Tesla endpoints omit methods=['POST']
items.evidence: State-mutating endpoints request_ro_deposit (api/payments.py:258), cancel_ro_deposit_request (api/payments.py:268), import_tesla_procedure (api/tesla.py:88), and link_vehicle_customer (api/tesla.py:471) use bare @frappe.whitelist() instead of @frappe.whitelist(methods=['POST']). By default Frappe accepts HTTP GET on whitelisted methods and skips CSRF validation for GET requests, unlike submit_square_payment (api/payments.py:303) which explicitly enforces methods=['POST'].
items.proposed_fix: Verify all Desk JS and MCP callers issue POST requests (repair_order.js uses frappe.call POST by default), then restrict request_ro_deposit, cancel_ro_deposit_request, import_tesla_procedure, and link_vehicle_customer to @frappe.whitelist(methods=['POST']).

items.title: ISM Technician bypasses /tech zero-pricing and role isolation via ism.api.agent.* endpoints
items.evidence: ISM Technician has DocType read+write on Repair Order (required for /tech execution) and read+write on Repair Vehicle (with no permission_query_conditions). Advisor/manager endpoints in agent_quotes.py (toggle_service_completion:L1231, amend_quote:L777, send_quote_for_approval:L859, add_supplement:L1350, duplicate_service_for_opposite_side:L1395, update_job_status:L931, get_deferred_services:L1423, add_deferred_services:L1477) and agent_fleet.py (get_vehicle_intelligence:L516, link_vehicle_customer:L548, apply_inspection_template:L655, record_check_in_inspection:L716) never call ism.permissions.is_manager_or_advisor(). On any assigned ready RO, a technician can directly invoke toggle_service_completion/add_supplement/amend_quote to receive _serialize_ro_compact(ro) with full pricing (grand_total, labor_rate, parts_total, discount_amount, deposit_amount), invoke send_quote_for_approval to generate/read customer approval_token and trigger SMS/email, or invoke update_job_status(action='complete'/'hold'). For ANY vehicle in the shop (even unassigned), a technician can call get_vehicle_intelligence or get_deferred_services(vehicle=...) to leak estimated_amount pricing, owner details, and unassigned RO references.
items.proposed_fix: Introduce a centralized require_manager_or_advisor() guard (delegating to ism.permissions.is_manager_or_advisor()) and enforce it at the start of advisor/manager-only endpoints in agent_quotes.py and agent_fleet.py while keeping ism.api.tech.* as the sole scoped, price-free technician API.

items.title: amend_quote allows unauthorized service additions and order-level fee tampering on Partially Approved and closed/billed ROs
items.evidence: Lines 799-807 check only `ro.docstatus != 0 or ro.approval_status == 'Approved' or (ro.approval_status == 'Partially Approved' and (not has_updates or bool(validated_remove)))`. First, Repair Order is non-submittable (is_submittable=0, docstatus always 0) and ro.status is never checked, allowing amendments on Billed / Paid, Closed / Released, or Cancelled ROs whenever approval_status != 'Approved'. Second, on a Partially Approved RO, supplying any unapproved row in update_services makes has_updates=True and bypasses the guard, letting the same request simultaneously execute add_services (L820-829) and mutate RO-level discount_amount, shop_supplies_amount, and environmental_fee_amount (L834-841) without customer re-authorization.
items.proposed_fix: Unconditionally reject amend_quote when ro.status in ('Billed / Paid', 'Closed / Released', 'Cancelled'). When ro.approval_status == 'Partially Approved', also reject if add_services, remove_service_indices, discount_amount, shop_supplies_amount, or environmental_fee_amount are provided (allowing only in-place updates on unapproved rows).

notes.text: Assigned in run-002
Fixed by fixer-a (amend_quote terminal status + Partially Approved guard); verified PASS by cross-family verifier (77/77 tests on slot-3).

items.title: tech.list_my_jobs applies LIMIT 500 across mixed active and completed records, starving active jobs under production history
items.evidence: Lines 584-657 fetch active ('Authorized - In Progress') and historical completed ('Work Completed', 'Billed / Paid') ROs together with limit_page_length=500 and no order_by before splitting in Python (L686-687); once >500 Billed / Paid ROs accumulate, active ROs are truncated past row 500 for managers. Worse, lines 660-684 query unlinked Schedule Entries with `status IN ('Scheduled','Confirmed','In Progress','Completed') ORDER BY scheduled_date ASC, scheduled_time ASC LIMIT 500`; once 500 historical Completed unlinked appointments exist, the oldest 500 Completed rows fill LIMIT 500 and ALL current/upcoming active appointments vanish from /tech for both managers and long-tenured technicians.
items.proposed_fix: Compute active_count and completed_count with targeted COUNT(*) queries, then fetch only ACTIVE_* statuses when include_completed=False (ordered ascending by scheduled date/time) and COMPLETED_* statuses when include_completed=True (ordered descending by modified / scheduled_date DESC, scheduled_time DESC).

items.title: agent_quotes.toggle_service_completion diverges from controller logic, drops side effects, lacks terminal-status lock, and breaks on docstatus=1
items.evidence: Unlike tech.toggle_service_item (which calls ro.toggle_service_completion -> fulfillment.py:toggle_ro_service_completion), agent_quotes.py:L1231-1321 reimplements toggling inline: (1) when transitioning ro.status to 'Work Completed' (L1301-1305) it never calls complete_linked_schedule_entries(), _maybe_send_ready_for_pickup_sms(), or _publish_ro_execution_updated(), leaving schedule entries open and /tech+/board desynced; (2) it has no guard against terminal RO statuses ('Billed / Paid', 'Closed / Released', 'Cancelled'), allowing mutation of billed/released ROs; (3) lines 1280-1321 execute direct db_set writes for ro.docstatus == 1 and then unconditionally call ro.save() on L1321, which throws UpdateAfterSubmitError after partial DB writes.
items.proposed_fix: Reject terminal statuses ('Billed / Paid', 'Closed / Released', 'Cancelled') and delegate execution (including batch service toggles, schedule-entry completion, pickup SMS, and realtime broadcast) to a single shared helper in Repair Order fulfillment so agent_quotes and tech.py cannot diverge.

items.title: _compute_batch_parts_summaries includes Billed / Paid ROs in FIFO stock commitments, causing false cockpit parts deficits
items.evidence: Lines 115-124 query fifo_ros with `status NOT IN ('Closed / Released', 'Cancelled')`, omitting 'Billed / Paid'. Per ism/ism/doctype/repair_order/billing.py:L776,L890, invoicing a Repair Order posts a submitted Sales Invoice with update_stock=1, which already deducts parts from Bin.actual_qty. Keeping 'Billed / Paid' ROs in fifo_ros deducts their required parts a second time from actual_by_wh (L220-233), permanently generating false has_stock_deficit / has_uncovered_deficit alerts on subsequent active ROs in /cockpit.
items.proposed_fix: Exclude 'Billed / Paid' from fifo_ros status filters (`['not in', ['Billed / Paid', 'Closed / Released', 'Cancelled']]`) and align with Repair Order stock-issued state so already-invoiced ROs do not consume live FIFO stock twice.

notes.text: Assigned in run-002
Fixed by fixer-a (exclude Billed / Paid and submitted update_stock Sales Invoice ROs from FIFO deduction); verified PASS by cross-family verifier (77/77 tests on slot-3).

items.title: get_pnl_digest_inputs includes Period Closing Voucher GL entries and aggregates raw GL Entry rows in Python
items.evidence: Lines 790-816 fetch every raw GL Entry row for [start_date, end_date] via unbounded frappe.get_all('GL Entry', ...) into Python and sum income/expense in a Python loop without filtering out `voucher_type = 'Period Closing Voucher'` or `is_opening = 'Yes'`. Any period spanning a fiscal year-end Period Closing Voucher zeros out gl_income and gl_expense in the digest. Fetching every raw GL Entry row into memory also causes O(N) latency and worker memory spikes on multi-month/annual queries.
items.proposed_fix: Replace the raw GL Entry + Account fetch and Python loop with a single parameterized SQL/frappe.qb query joining `tabGL Entry` to `tabAccount` with `is_cancelled = 0`, `IFNULL(is_opening, 'No') = 'No'`, `IFNULL(voucher_type, '') != 'Period Closing Voucher'`, and `root_type IN ('Income', 'Expense')`, aggregating `SUM(credit - debit)` with `GROUP BY root_type`.

items.title: find_available_slots returns past dates and elapsed today slots when include_past=False
items.evidence: Lines 299-306 iterate `window.iter_dates()` (which yields all dates from start_dt..end_dt without checking today_dt) and only set `day_min_time = now_time_str` in `elif not allow_past and cur_dt == today_dt:`. Consequently, with include_past=False (default): (1) passing a past start_date yields all slots on dates < today_dt with day_min_time=None; (2) passing start_date=today with an earlier min_start_time hits the `if norm_min_time and cur_dt == start_dt:` branch first and skips the `now_time_str` floor, returning already-elapsed morning slots.
items.proposed_fix: When `not allow_past`, skip any `cur_dt < today_dt` (`continue`), and on `cur_dt == today_dt`, clamp `day_min_time` to `max(norm_min_time, now_time_str)` when `norm_min_time` is provided for `start_dt`.

items.title: receive_purchase_order silently truncates partial/multi-invoice PO receipts and lacks row locking or cancelled-PO guard
items.evidence: Lines 884-924 lack a `FOR UPDATE` row lock on Purchase Order/Invoice (exposing concurrent double-receipt races) and never reject `po.docstatus == 2` (Cancelled) or `po.status in ('Closed', 'On Hold')` upfront. In Scenario A (L903-924), when receiving by purchase_order alone, `limit_page_length=1` picks only the first linked unreceived Purchase Invoice and maps the Purchase Receipt from that single PI; if a PO was partially invoiced or billed across multiple PIs, remaining PO lines or sibling PIs are silently skipped while returning success=True.
items.proposed_fix: Acquire a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` row lock on Purchase Order before validating docstatus/status/per_received, reject Cancelled/Closed/On Hold POs explicitly, and only auto-route Scenario A through `make_pr_from_pi` when exactly one unreceived PI matches 100% of the PO's remaining receivable quantities (otherwise map from PO or raise a clear ValidationError listing the multiple PIs).

items.title: sync_action_item_state has an unlocked check-then-act race on non-unique dedup_key and dead skip_board_projection flag
items.evidence: Shop Action Item.dedup_key is indexed but not unique. agent_fleet.py:L311-356 queries `frappe.get_all('Shop Action Item', filters={'dedup_key': dedup_key}, limit_page_length=1)` without locking and then inserts a new row if empty; concurrent snooze/dismiss calls for the same dedup_key insert duplicate rows, splitting cockpit overlay state across workstations. Additionally, L355 sets `doc.flags.skip_board_projection = True`, which is never read by projections.py:on_shop_action_item_on_update.
items.proposed_fix: Wrap the lookup-and-upsert in a short distributed lock (`frappe.cache().lock(f'ism:sai_dedup:{dedup_key}', timeout=10)`) plus `FOR UPDATE` on the matched row, and remove the dead `skip_board_projection` assignment.

items.title: _compute_batch_parts_summaries _warehouse_for(None) cache-key mismatch causes repeated DB lookups in loops
items.evidence: Lines 169-172 check `if company not in wh_by_company:` but store under `wh_by_company[company or '']`. Whenever `company` is `None`, `None not in wh_by_company` is always True, defeating memoization and executing `_resolve_default_warehouse(None)` DB queries repeatedly on every iteration of the fifo_ros (L222) and active_ros (L251) loops.
items.proposed_fix: Normalize the cache key once via `key = company or ''` and check `if key not in wh_by_company: wh_by_company[key] = _resolve_default_warehouse(company)`.

items.title: Missing ISM Technician negative-authorization tests for ism.api.agent.* and monitoring edge-case coverage

items.title: Missing server-side CSRF and Origin validation on Guest cookie-authenticated mutating portal endpoints
items.evidence: api/portal.py:11 states mutating endpoints rely on Frappe CSRF protection and public/portal/api.js:154-157 sends X-Frappe-CSRF-Token, but Frappe skips validate_csrf_token whenever frappe.session.user == 'Guest'—the normal principal for all portal customers authenticated via the ism_portal_session cookie (default SameSite=Lax in comms/sessions.py:152). None of the 10 mutating POST endpoints (submit_portal_payment, submit_portal_quote_approval, submit_pin_to_drive, opt_out_pin_to_drive, submit_tesla_phone_key, remove_tesla_phone_key, reschedule_appointment, email_invoice_copy, sign_out, exchange_portal_link) verify X-Frappe-CSRF-Token, Origin, or Sec-Fetch-Site server-side, leaving authenticated mutations exposed to same-site subdomain or non-Lax CSRF.
items.proposed_fix: Add a shared server-side CSRF/Origin guard in portal/auth.py invoked on all mutating POST endpoints in api/portal.py when an HTTP request is active: require Origin (or Referer fallback) to match the request host (or Sec-Fetch-Site == 'same-origin') and verify X-Frappe-CSRF-Token against frappe.sessions.get_csrf_token() while preserving direct in-process Python test calls when frappe.local.request is absent. [Verifier caveat: frappe.sessions.get_csrf_token() is not persisted server-side for Guest sessions in Frappe, so Guest CSRF validation must use an HMAC token bound to ism_portal_session alongside Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site checks.]

items.title: Unescaped SSR Jinja interpolations and incomplete inline script JSON escaping across www/ and templates/pages/
items.evidence: Frappe renders Jinja .html pages with autoescape=False (evidenced by www/book.html:124 outputting raw JSON without | safe and www/portal.html:14 needing | forceescape). Consequently: (1) templates/pages/quote_approval.html:20-34,45-49 interpolates customer/RO-sourced veh.color, veh.model, veh.license_plate, veh.vin, veh.display, and approval_data.error unescaped (Stored XSS), and www/board.html:44-45,55, www/tech.html:35-36,46, www/cockpit.html:27, www/portal.html:18,21, and www/book.html:9,18-23,38-44,56,104,113-120 interpolate user_full_name, error_message, token_error, and shop/booking strings unescaped; (2) www/board.py:171 and www/tech.py:185 serialize boot_data (including reflected ?ro= query input in www/tech.py:126-128 and RO/thread strings in www/board.py:159-160) into inline <script> via .replace('</', '<\\/') only, leaving '<!-- <script>' unescaped and enabling HTML5 script-data escaped-state breakout.
items.proposed_fix: Apply explicit '| e' (or '| forceescape') to all dynamic text and attribute interpolations across quote_approval.html, portal.html, book.html, board.html, tech.html, and cockpit.html; consolidate _safe_json_for_script (escaping '<', '>', '&', '</', '\u2028', '\u2029') into ism/utils/web_security.py and use it in board.py, tech.py, cockpit.py, and book.py.

items.title: ISM Settings.enable_customer_portal kill switch is never enforced on any portal API or SSR route
items.evidence: portal/auth.py:295-296 reads ISM Settings.enable_customer_portal solely to populate branding['portal_enabled']. Unlike api/booking.py:_preflight_booking_enabled (which fails closed with HTTP 503 when booking is disabled), zero endpoints in api/portal.py (exchange_portal_link, request_login_otp, verify_login_otp, get_portal_hub, submit_portal_quote_approval, submit_pin_to_drive, submit_tesla_phone_key, get_reschedule_options, reschedule_appointment, submit_portal_payment, download_invoice_pdf, email_invoice_copy) and neither /portal nor /quote-approval enforce enable_customer_portal == 1. Turning off the Customer Portal in ISM Settings leaves all portal auth, PII reads, quote approvals, PIN/Phone Key writes, reschedules, and Square payments fully operational.
items.proposed_fix: Add assert_portal_enabled() in portal/auth.py (failing closed unless enable_customer_portal == 1 or demo_mode is active) and enforce it in exchange_portal_link, request_login_otp, verify_login_otp, require_portal_session, www/portal.py, and templates/pages/quote_approval.py while keeping get_portal_bootstrap returning {'authenticated': False, 'shop': {'portal_enabled': False, ...}}. [Verifier note: api/portal.py:161-182 (get_portal_bootstrap) calls get_active_portal_session directly rather than require_portal_session, so it must also short-circuit to {'authenticated': False, 'shop': branding} when portal_enabled is False.]

items.title: Deterministic phone-number enumeration oracle in portal OTP login verification and request flows
items.evidence: portal/auth.py:719-720 and L817 aim to prevent customer phone enumeration, but two deterministic response divergences leak customer existence with 100% accuracy: (1) in verify_portal_login_otp (auth.py:821-831), unknown-phone noop challenges delete the cache marker after max_attempts and return error_code='INVALID_CODE' without locked_until, whereas known-phone challenges (auth.py:857-865, forwarded verbatim by api/portal.py:274-277) return error_code='LOCKED_OUT' with locked_until on the 5th bad guess; (2) in request_portal_login_otp (auth.py:709-717 vs 719-789), known phones that are locked out or opted out return LOCKED_OUT/OPTED_OUT/DELIVERY_FAILED whereas unknown phones skip both checks and return success=True.
items.proposed_fix: Track per-phone synthetic lockout state in Redis for unknown-phone noop challenges (returning identical LOCKED_OUT + locked_until after max_attempts and enforcing it in request_portal_login_otp), and make unknown/known request_portal_login_otp responses uniform when opted out or locked out.

items.title: Defensive PIN and Phone Key vault purges on closed/cancelled records are rolled back on PermissionError
items.evidence: In pin_vault.py:525-532 (get_ro_pin_for_staff), pin_vault.py:932-939 (get_schedule_entry_pin_for_staff), phone_key_vault.py:490-501 (get_ro_phone_key_for_staff), and phone_key_vault.py:872-879 (get_schedule_entry_phone_key_for_staff), when a Closed/Released or Cancelled doc still has residual __Auth ciphertext, the function invokes purge_*() and immediately raises frappe.throw(..., frappe.PermissionError). In real HTTP requests, Frappe's exception handler rolls back the DB transaction on PermissionError, undoing the __Auth row deletion, status transition to Purged/Released, and audit Comment. Unit test test_portal_pin_vault.py:534-544 missed this because it calls Python directly without HTTP rollback.
items.proposed_fix: Commit the defensive purge before throwing (when not inside a unit-test transaction, or via a dedicated commit helper matching www/portal.py) so residual __Auth ciphertext stays permanently deleted even after raising PermissionError, and add a rollback-simulating regression test.

items.title: Desk PIN and Phone Key reveal endpoints permit HTTP GET and omit Cache-Control: no-store headers
items.evidence: Unlike api/portal.py:781-802 (which enforces allow_guest=False, methods=['POST']), the four Desk-whitelisted endpoints—pin_vault.py:610 (reveal_ro_pin_desk), pin_vault.py:1021 (reveal_schedule_entry_pin_desk), phone_key_vault.py:580 (reveal_ro_phone_key_desk), and phone_key_vault.py:961 (reveal_schedule_entry_phone_key_desk)—use bare @frappe.whitelist() without methods=['POST']. This allows GET requests that mutate audit state (incrementing *_view_count and inserting Comments without Frappe POST CSRF protection) and risk caching plaintext 4-digit PINs and Tesla Phone Key URLs in browser/proxy caches. Moreover, none of the 8 staff reveal endpoints set Cache-Control: private, no-store, max-age=0. [Verifier severity confirmation: Frappe does not auto-commit DB writes on HTTP GET, so GET requests to *_desk return plaintext PIN/Phone Key while silently dropping the *_view_count increment and audit Comment.]
items.proposed_fix: Restrict all four *_desk reveal endpoints to @frappe.whitelist(methods=['POST']) (verifying Desk callers use POST) and set Cache-Control: private, no-store, max-age=0 and Pragma: no-cache on frappe.local.response_headers inside get_ro_pin_for_staff, get_schedule_entry_pin_for_staff, get_ro_phone_key_for_staff, and get_schedule_entry_phone_key_for_staff.

items.title: Plaintext 30-day bearer booking_token URL persisted unredacted in SMS Audit Log
items.evidence: portal/auth.py:241-286 (create_booking_portal_link) hashes the 256-bit booking token with SHA-256 on Schedule Entry specifically so DB/staff access cannot forge customer portal sessions. However, booking/service.py:1310-1325 sends sms_body containing the live ?booking_token=<raw_token> URL via send_sms(SMSDispatchRequest(..., redact_body=False)) with no redacted_preview. In comms/providers.py:477-497, _write_sms_audit_log writes request.body verbatim to SMS Audit Log.message_preview (retained 180 days per hooks.py:324), exposing active bearer session-minting tokens in plaintext.
items.proposed_fix: Pass redact_body=True and an explicit redacted_preview replacing the booking_token query parameter with [REDACTED] (e.g. '/portal?booking_token=[REDACTED]') in booking/service.py:1316-1324 so the outbound SMS delivers the clickable link while SMS Audit Log never persists the raw token. [Verifier note: redact_otp_body (comms/contracts.py:223-230) only masks 4-8 digit runs, so passing an explicit redacted_preview stripping ?booking_token=<raw_token> alongside redact_body=True is required.]

items.title: exchange_ro_approval_token fails open when Repair Order.approval_token_expiry is NULL
items.evidence: portal/auth.py:579 checks 'if row.get("approval_token_expiry") and now_datetime() > get_datetime(row["approval_token_expiry"]):', which evaluates to False whenever approval_token_expiry is None/NULL. Any Repair Order with an approval_token but missing expiry therefore accepts token exchange indefinitely to mint 30-day Customer Portal Session cookies, contradicting exchange_booking_token (portal/auth.py:635-637) which fails closed with 'if not expires_at or now_datetime() > get_datetime(expires_at):'. [Verifier calibration (high->medium): Sole production issuer issue_approval_token (repair_order/authorization.py:336-337) always populates approval_token_expiry and both fields are read_only=1 in repair_order.json:397,405, limiting exposure to direct DB/ORM writes or imports. Note the same fail-open pattern exists out-of-zone in api/approval.py:160,343 and api/payments.py:154.]
items.proposed_fix: Change portal/auth.py:579 to fail closed when approval_token_expiry is missing ('if not row.get("approval_token_expiry") or now_datetime() > get_datetime(row["approval_token_expiry"]):') and add a unit test asserting NULL-expiry RO tokens are rejected.

items.title: Concurrent lazy Fernet key generation in _get_pin_fernet risks overwriting key and stranding vault ciphertexts
items.evidence: pin_vault.py:104-139 (_get_pin_fernet, also used by phone_key_vault.py:116-119) checks get_decrypted_password for ISM Settings.portal_pin_encryption_key without acquiring any lock; when blank, it calls Fernet.generate_key() and writes it to __Auth and tabSingles. Under concurrent first-write requests on an unseeded or key-cleared site, Worker A encrypts a PIN/Phone Key with Key A while Worker B overwrites __Auth with Key B, permanently stranding Worker A's ciphertext with InvalidToken decryption failures.
items.proposed_fix: Acquire a FOR UPDATE lock on the ISM Settings tabSingles row (or a short Redis/MySQL lock) and re-check get_decrypted_password inside the lock before generating and persisting portal_pin_encryption_key.

items.title: Opposite Repair Order <-> Schedule Entry FOR UPDATE lock ordering across vault operations risks InnoDB deadlocks
items.evidence: on_repair_order_update_purge_pin (pin_vault.py:685,728) locks tabRepair Order first (purge_ro_pin) and then locks linked tabSchedule Entry rows (purge_schedule_entry_pin / purge_schedule_entry_phone_key). In contrast, transfer_schedule_entry_pin_to_ro (pin_vault.py:1034-1035), transfer_schedule_entry_phone_key_to_ro (phone_key_vault.py:974-975), submit_schedule_entry_pin (pin_vault.py:828-831), opt_out_schedule_entry_pin (L876-879), get_schedule_entry_pin_for_staff (L919-922), and the matching Schedule Entry functions in phone_key_vault.py lock tabSchedule Entry first and tabRepair Order second. Concurrent RO release/cancellation and SE credential submit/reveal/transfer can trigger InnoDB deadlocks.
items.proposed_fix: Standardize canonical cross-table lock ordering (Repair Order before Schedule Entry): in transfer_schedule_entry_*_to_ro lock ro before se, and in submit_/opt_out_/remove_/get_schedule_entry_* read repair_order non-locking first, lock Repair Order if linked, and only lock Schedule Entry when unlinked or after RO lock.

items.title: TOCTOU race on booking daily/duplicate phone limits and unvalidated demo-* challenge bypass in verify_and_commit_booking
items.evidence: Two booking anti-abuse gaps in booking/service.py:1159-1274: (1) check_phone_daily_limit_and_duplicate (service.py:1189-1195, anti_abuse.py:270-324) runs BEFORE create_provisional_booking acquires Service Bay/Employee locks and record_phone_daily_booking runs AFTER insert (L1274). Because request_sms_otp only supersedes Pending challenges (comms/otp.py:469) leaving Verified challenges live, concurrent confirm_self_serve_booking requests for the same phone read the same pre-commit snapshot and bypass both phone_rate_limit_per_day and max_concurrent_bookings_per_phone; (2) when demo_mode is enabled, is_demo_bypass = booking_settings.demo_mode and clean_challenge_id.startswith('demo-') (L1159) accepts any arbitrary fabricated 'demo-*' string directly without verifying initiate_booking_otp issued it or checking otp_code, while bypassing IP/phone/duplicate limits.
items.proposed_fix: Guard check_phone_daily_limit_and_duplicate + commit with a per-phone lock (or re-check under lock inside create_provisional_booking) and atomically reserve/rollback the daily Redis counter; in demo_mode, store issued demo-* challenge IDs in cache bound to phone_e164 with TTL and require otp_code == '000000' before committing.

items.title: Non-SARGable 6-table REGEXP_REPLACE full table scans executed up to 3x per customer-scoped portal request
items.evidence: resolve_subjects_for_phone (portal/auth.py:426-545) runs 6 SQL queries filtering RIGHT(REGEXP_REPLACE(<phone_col>, '[^0-9]', ''), %s) = %s across tabCustomer, tabContact, tabContact Phone, and tabSchedule Entry, preventing MariaDB index usage and causing 6 full table scans per call. On customer-scoped portal mutations (e.g. api/portal.py:317,344 submit_portal_quote_approval, submit_pin_to_drive, submit_portal_payment), assert_session_owns_ro calls list_accessible_visit_keys -> resolve_subjects_for_phone once in the endpoint, a second time inside build_portal_hub_payload (visit_view.py:418), and a third time at visit_view.py:430—executing 18 full table scans in a single HTTP request.
items.proposed_fix: Pass a precomputed accessible visit-key dict (or request-scoped memoization keyed by session_id + phone_e164) from api/portal.py into assert_session_owns_* and build_portal_hub_payload to eliminate redundant 3x calls immediately; follow up with a planned schema migration adding indexed normalized phone-suffix columns/indexes.

items.title: reschedule_appointment fails for logged-in Website Users and OTP scope upgrade drops sms_otp audit metadata
items.evidence: (1) api/portal.py:614-616 elevates to Administrator only when prev_user == 'Guest' (unlike booking/service.py:169-172 which elevates whenever prev_user != 'Administrator'). Any customer logged into Frappe as a Website User (or non-privileged Desk user) who reschedules via /portal hits PermissionError inside ScheduleEntry.validate() -> check_bay_availability(); (2) in portal/auth.py:880-887, upgrading a magic_link session to scope_type='customer' via SMS OTP calls rotate_portal_session(customer=primary_customer, scope_type='customer'), which in comms/sessions.py:597-603 preserves the old auth_method='magic_link' and source_otp_challenge=None (and retains stale row.customer if primary_customer is None), misrecording customer-wide OTP upgrades in the session audit log.
items.proposed_fix: Elevate whenever prev_user != 'Administrator' (with guaranteed finally restore) in api/portal.py:614-627 matching booking/service.py; extend rotate_portal_session / portal/auth.py:880-887 to update auth_method='sms_otp', source_otp_challenge=source_challenge_id, and explicit customer/schedule_entry values during OTP upgrade.

items.title: Unthrottled synchronous wkhtmltopdf PDF generation on download_invoice_pdf enables worker DoS
items.evidence: Unlike email_invoice_copy (rate-limited via Project 1 email dispatch) and exchange_portal_link (30/min IP & token bucket), download_invoice_pdf (api/portal.py:726-750) imposes zero rate limiting before calling frappe.get_print('Sales Invoice', si_name, as_pdf=True) (invoices.py:173-187), which spawns CPU/memory-intensive wkhtmltopdf subprocesses synchronously on Gunicorn workers. Any holder of a single valid magic link or portal session can flood GET downloads to saturate workers and host memory.
items.proposed_fix: Enforce a Redis-backed per-IP and per-session rate limit (e.g. 20 downloads/minute) in api/portal.py:download_invoice_pdf raising frappe.TooManyRequestsError before rendering the Sales Invoice PDF. [Verifier note: Clear the new Redis bucket prefix inside clear_portal_auth_rate_limits so tests stay hermetic.]

items.title: Cross-RO IDOR in post_board_capture duplicate idempotency_key fallback
items.evidence: Lines 1107-1120 check assert_can_access_ro(existing_thread.repair_order, user=caller_user) before returning a pre-existing idempotency_key event, but the DuplicateEntryError/UniqueValidationError fallback at L1194-1208 runs inside _as_system_user() and returns _serialize_event(existing_doc) without checking assert_can_access_ro on existing_doc.repair_order (and returns the caller's thread_doc instead of existing_doc.thread). [Cross-family verifier calibration: downgraded high -> medium because the unguarded fallback is only reachable during a sub-millisecond concurrent insert race on Shop Board Event.idempotency_key.]
items.proposed_fix: In L1194-1208, load existing_thread = frappe.get_doc('Shop Board Thread', existing_doc.thread), enforce assert_can_access_ro(existing_thread.repair_order, user=caller_user) when existing_thread.repair_order is set, and return _serialize_thread(existing_thread). Add a regression test simulating DuplicateEntryError across ROs for an ISM Technician user.

items.title: recompute_thread_projection increments projection_version without FOR UPDATE lock
items.evidence: recompute_thread_projection loads Shop Board Thread via frappe.get_doc (L239), computes new_version = cint(thread.projection_version or 0) + 1 (L312), and persists via thread.db_set (L316) without locking the thread row. Concurrent capture/RO/AI updates can compute identical projection_version values, overwrite fresher Andon status, and cause get_thread_delta clients to miss deltas. [Cross-family verifier confirmed: Shop Board Thread is always the leaf lock after Repair Order / Shop Action Item / Shop Board Event writes, so SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on primary key name is deadlock-free.]
items.proposed_fix: Execute SELECT projection_version, board_status, blocked_since FROM `tabShop Board Thread` WHERE name = %s FOR UPDATE at the start of recompute_thread_projection and compute new_version/prev_status/prev_blocked_since from the locked row.

items.title: get_thread_delta polling endpoint runs mutating sweep_open_action_items on every poll
items.evidence: get_thread_delta (L882-913) is a high-frequency polling endpoint that synchronously invokes sweep_open_action_items(repair_order=thread_doc.repair_order, limit=50) (clearing.py:725-785) on every poll, performing N+1 Shop Action Item loads, PO/PR/SMS/Communication queries, and item_doc.save() writes on read traffic even though clearing hooks already run on document updates.
items.proposed_fix: Throttle or remove the synchronous sweep from get_thread_delta (e.g., per-RO Redis cooldown of 30-60s or rely on reactive doc hooks + initial get_board_thread sweep) after confirming no UI flow depends on unhooked clearing conditions during delta polls.

items.title: Sales Invoice ignores explicit non-zero ro.tax_rate when default tax template is attached
items.evidence: pricing.py:388-409 calculates ro.total_taxes_and_charges and ro.grand_total from explicit ro.tax_rate (e.g. 5.0%) even when ro.taxes_and_charges holds the default 13% HST template. In billing.py:873-881 and L1121-1139, only explicit_zero_tax (0.0) skips si.set_taxes(); any non-zero custom ro.tax_rate loads the 13% template rate into si.taxes, skips the L1127 fallback, and invoices a different grand_total than the customer authorized.
items.proposed_fix: After si.set_taxes() at L1122, when ro.tax_rate is explicitly set (> 0) and si.taxes has a single 'On Net Total' row whose rate differs from flt(ro.tax_rate), align si.taxes[0].rate to flt(ro.tax_rate) (and update si.taxes[0].description accordingly) so Sales Invoice totals match the authorized Repair Order. Add a regression test in test_repair_order.py.

items.title: Customer approval silently succeeds and notifies shop floor when zero pending services match
items.evidence: In authorization.py:419-438, if an explicit approvals dict matches no pending service row on a multi-service RO, newly_approved and newly_declined are both empty; L462 skips signature/audit log creation, L499 still saves and returns status='success', and api/approval.py:294-303 emits _notify_shop_floor_approval and returns success=True to the customer despite zero services changing state. [Cross-family verifier regression guard: test_repair_order.py:1447-1454 calls ro.authorize_jobs(...) directly on an already-decided RO (has_pending == False) and expects a locked no-op without raising ValidationError.]
items.proposed_fix: Scope the ValidationError guard to is_public_portal / authorize_ro_for_portal (or only when pending services exist on the RO and an explicit approvals payload matches zero pending rows), throwing frappe.ValidationError instead of returning success and notifying the shop floor — while preserving the locked no-op contract on already-decided ROs tested by test_repair_order.py:1447. Add a regression test in test_approval_and_inspection.py.

items.title: Public approval portal rate limiter uses non-atomic get-then-set and extends TTL on every hit
items.evidence: _increment_rate_limit_key (L51-60) reads cache.get_value(cache_key) and writes current+1 via cache.set_value(..., expires_in_sec=window_sec). Concurrent bursts race past the limit, and resetting expires_in_sec on every hit (including rejected calls) causes indefinite lockout for retrying clients.
items.proposed_fix: Use atomic Redis INCR on cache.make_key(cache_key) (keeping delete_keys / clear_portal_rate_limits() key-compatible) and set EXPIRE only when count == 1, preserving a safe fallback if the cache client lacks incr. Add a unit test in test_approval_and_inspection.py.

items.title: estimate_repair_order executes empirical percentile DB lookup inside per-service loop
items.evidence: In estimate_repair_order (L681-703), when empirical=True, _compute_empirical_percentile_minutes (estimation_service.py:222-285) is called inside the `for s in services:` loop, issuing per-service frappe.qb join queries against `tabRepair Order Service` rather than batching by all service packages/titles.
items.proposed_fix: Prefetch empirical duration samples across all service_package and service_title keys in a single query before the loop and pass the prefetched map into _compute_empirical_percentile_minutes.
